name: arm_sync_file_range
synopsis: int arm_sync_file_range(int fd, off_t offset, off_t nbytes, unsigned int flags);
description: arm_sync_file_range() provides fine control for synchronizing a specified range of an open file with disk on ARM architectures. It synchronizes the range starting from offset for nbytes bytes, with behavior controlled by flags. This call is architecture-specific and should be used cautiously due to potential data integrity risks.

parameters.name: fd
parameters.description: File descriptor of the open file to synchronize.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Starting byte of the file range to synchronize; rounded down to a page boundary.

parameters.name: nbytes
parameters.description: Length of the range to synchronize; if zero, synchronizes from offset to the end of the file.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Bit-mask of flags, such as SYNC_FILE_RANGE_WAIT_BEFORE, SYNC_FILE_RANGE_WRITE, or SYNC_FILE_RANGE_WAIT_AFTER, to control the synchronization behavior.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: fd is not a valid file descriptor.
flags specifies an invalid bit; or offset or nbytes is invalid.
fd refers to something other than a regular file, a block device, or a directory.

bugs: This system call is extremely dangerous and should not be used in portable programs, as it does not write out file metadata, may not ensure data integrity after a crash, and does not flush disk write caches.
